subject: journey/alexander
prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset: ONE landscape 3:2 campaign sketchbook page.
An illustrated page from an explorer's journal: one particular moment on the journey, drawn close enough to see faces, hands, tools, clothing and the things being traded, measured or found. The traveller need not appear: some pages record only what the party saw (a harbour, a fortress, a market, an animal or plant). When the traveller does appear, draw them in action and in a natural, varied pose, not standing to attention. In the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries. A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink with loose hatching; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green, faded blue and a touch of red. The page may carry one or two small separate studies of a detail (an object, a tool, a creature) loosely arranged beside the main scene, as on a real sketchbook page. Edges unfinished, dissolving into bare, slightly foxed cream paper; a single page, no binding visible. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, numbers, dates or signature; any writing that appears in the scene is illegible marks. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given; people, dress and objects true to their place and time, drawn with respect.
Scene date: 324 BCE. Location: Susa.
Subject and viewpoint: Side view of restrained Susa Persian court wedding ceremony 324 BCE, one adult Macedonian officer seated beside adult Persian noblewoman in long modest draped dress and veil, attendants presenting small cup, other couples small receding under palace colonnade. No white Western bridal gowns crosses crowns or modern banquet, respectful adult faces, no mandatory Alexander.
Character continuity only if required: Alexander of Macedon, aged22 at departure in334BCE and32 in323BCE, young adult man with light olive skin, wavy light-brown hair swept back from forehead, clean-shaven, lean athletic build. Plain off-white short tunic and muted red travel cloak, practical fourth-century BCE Macedonian armor only when appropriate. Never medieval crown, Roman segmented armor or stirrups. Troops and local people have varied faces, ages and dress appropriate to each region. Alexander appears only when the scene explicitly asks for him.
No recurring hero if not requested. Use ancient materials and coherent object geometry, anatomically correct hands and animals. Keep this a loose observed sketch with irregular cream paper margins, not polished fantasy concept art. No readable text, labels or map lettering.
